children: Definitive Healthcare named Clay Ritchey as its new chief executive, effective Sept. 8, succeeding Kevin Coop, who departed Aug. 31.

The healthcare data company said Coop's departure wasn't the result of a disagreement on any matter relating to its operations, policies, or practices. Coop, who will also leave the board, had served as chief executive since June 2024.

Ritchey joins after most recently serving as chief executive of Verato, a healthcare master data management company. He has also worked as CEO of Evariant prior to its acquisition by Healthgrades and CEO of Equinox Healthcare.

Definitive Healthcare plans to pay Ritchey an annual base salary of $500,000, plus annual bonuses and equity awards. In connection with his appointment, Ritchey will receive equity awards with an aggregate target grant date value of $4 million.
Separately on Wednesday, Definitive Healthcare said it received an indication of interest from Advent International, a private equity firm that wants to buy the company for $1.02 a share.
